endorsements.quote: Addressing these challenges will require not only fairness-aware model development, but also rigorous uncertainty quantification, calibration and prospective evaluation across diverse real-world settings.

Before biomedical world models are deployed to guide scientific or clinical decisionmaking, their simulated trajectories, intervention recommendations and downstream outcomes must be systematically validated against experimental and clinical evidence.

unlisted_practices: Develop multi-dimensional evaluation frameworks for biomedical world models that assess observational realism, state consistency, temporal coherence, interventional accuracy, counterfactual validity and planning utility.
Assess temporal stability and robustness under intervention in long-horizon simulations, not only local predictive accuracy.
Build community-level benchmarking infrastructure, including open benchmark suites, shared tasks, hidden test sets and transparent leaderboards.
Build longitudinal, intervention-aware data infrastructure with temporal alignment, quality control and harmonization across modalities and institutions.
Use standardized biomedical ontologies and coding systems to align heterogeneous biomedical data into interoperable representations.
Use privacy-preserving strategies such as federated learning, secure computation, differential privacy and encrypted data processing for collaborative model training across institutions.
Combine technical privacy protections with transparent data governance and auditable access control.
Document data sources, model limitations and intended use cases clearly.
Specify standardized operation interfaces for world-model-driven systems, covering state representations, available actions, logging mechanisms, rollback procedures and human oversight points.
Adopt fairness-aware model development for biomedical world models.
Consider environmental impact in training and deploying large biomedical world models.
Use efficient modelling techniques such as distillation, pruning and quantization to lower cost and enable deployment in low-resource settings.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/framework paper proposing biomedical world models for simulation and outlining required governance frameworks and safety constraints, rather than an empirical evaluation.
